text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.8% today to $125.27, extending a sharp two-week decline as oil prices dropped for a fifth consecutive day on signs of potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress. Reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz (a critical global oil chokepoint) within a week if the U.S. eases military pressure have eased concerns about immediate supply disruptions, which earlier this month had helped push oil higher. The gap between U.S. crude ($107/barrel) and global prices ($131/barrel) also narrowed, suggesting less urgency about potential shortages.

Beyond today's diplomacy headlines, the stock has been pressured by broader geopolitical uncertainty and political discussion about a potential diesel export ban—moves aimed at lowering fuel costs for farmers and truckers. With Wall Street itself uncertain where oil prices are headed amid shifting Iran negotiations and supply dynamics, energy producers like ConocoPhillips remain caught between hopes for diplomatic resolution (which would weigh on prices) and fears of supply disruption (which would support them).
